# QA Report — Sidebar Hierarchy & Default-Project Naming

## VERDICT: **FAIL** — 3 of 3 acceptance criteria fail

Suite is green and the build is clean, but the green tests certify the *opposite* of the requested behavior. Nothing was edited, staged, or committed.

---

## Commands & Exit Codes

| Command (cwd `ui/`) | Exit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `bun x vitest run src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/components/Sidebar.activity.test.tsx src/components/WorktreeList.test.tsx` | **0** | 25 passed |
| `bun x vitest run src/App.test.tsx` | **0** | 18 passed |
| `bun x tsc --noEmit` | **0** | clean typecheck |
| `bun run build` (`tsc && vite build`) | **0** | built in 1.68s |
| `bun x vitest run` (5 files, final sweep) | **0** | 53 passed, 0 failed |

Read-only confirmed: `git status --short -- ui/src src-tauri/src` shows the same 52 pre-existing entries before and after. `ui/dist/` was regenerated by the build and is gitignored (`.gitignore:11`).

---

## Criterion 1 — "Titlebar contains no Add Worktree" → **FAIL**

`ui/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:169` places Add Worktree *inside* the titlebar drag region:

```tsx
<IconButton label="Add worktree" className="no-drag" size="sm" onClick={() => onCreateWorktree()}>
```

It sits in the `data-testid="sidebar-drag-region"` / `data-tauri-drag-region` container beside Hide sidebar and Add project. The diff did the reverse of the requirement: it *deleted* the `SectionHeader` Add Worktree and *promoted* it to the titlebar. `Sidebar.test.tsx:95` locks this in:

```js
fireEvent.click(within(titlebar).getByRole("button", { name: "Add worktree" }));
expect(onCreateWorktree).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
```

That handler calls `onCreateWorktree()` with **no argument**, so it targets whatever `activeProject` happens to be (`App.tsx:611`).

## Criterion 2 — "Each project row shows an Add Worktree affordance opening creation for that exact project" → **FAIL**

No such affordance exists. The project row (`Sidebar.tsx:202-253`) renders exactly two children: the chevron toggle and the project-select button. A `group/project` hover class was added at line 204 — clearly staged for a hover-revealed button — but the button was never written.

The only per-project creation path is the `"Create the first worktree"` link in `WorktreeList.tsx:47`, rendered **only when `worktrees.length === 0`**. Any project with ≥1 worktree has no per-project Add Worktree at all.

Plumbing is correct as far as it goes: `Sidebar.tsx:263` passes `onCreate={() => onCreateWorktree(project)}`, `App.tsx:610-613` sets `createTargetProject`, and `AddWorktreeDialog` scopes to `project.workspaceId` (`ProjectDialogs.tsx:296-297`). The wiring works; the entry point is missing.

## Criterion 3 — "Initial project displays repository folder-derived ID rather than default" → **FAIL**

`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-155` correctly derives and registers a slugged folder ID, but the sidebar never sees it:

1. **UI hardcodes `"default"`.** `App.tsx:52` defines `DEFAULT_PROJECT = { workspaceId: DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID, repoRoot: "." }` with `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID = "default"` (`lib/tauri.ts:19`). `loadProjects()` (`App.tsx:761-774`) returns `[DEFAULT_PROJECT]` on **every** miss path — no storage, unparseable JSON, empty array, throw. Fresh install renders the row as literally **"default"**.
2. **No IPC exposes the registry.** `rg listProjects|cmd_project_list|project_list` across `ui/src` and `src-tauri/src` = zero matches. `WorkspaceRegistry::list()` (`registry.rs:58`) has no command surface, so the derived ID is unreachable from the frontend by construction.

`lib.rs:152-154` also **still registers `"default"`** at the same repo root, so the hardcoded UI ID resolves successfully and the defect fails silently instead of erroring.

---

## Test-Coverage Gaps

- `Sidebar.test.tsx:262` asserts only `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` — never *which* project was passed. It would pass identically if the wrong project were routed.
- `App.test.tsx:166` renders a mocked `"Add worktree to {workspaceId}"` button that **no test ever clicks** — dead scaffolding, zero coverage of per-project targeting.
- `rg derived_id` matches only the four `lib.rs` implementation lines — zero Rust tests. `App.test.tsx:75` mocks `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID: "default"`, pinning pre-change behavior.

---

## UI Automation Limitation

I cannot drive the user's desktop UI: no Tauri window was launched, no native-window automation or screenshots. All evidence is jsdom-rendered React plus static source inspection.

- **Criterion 1 — fully covered.** Titlebar composition is pure DOM structure; `within(titlebar).getByRole(...)` is authoritative.
- **Criterion 2 — fully covered for the failure.** Absence of an element in rendered output is conclusive. jsdom cannot verify CSS hover reveal, but that is moot: nothing exists to reveal.
- **Criterion 3 — partially covered.** The `"default"` seeding and missing IPC command are proven statically and are conclusive; a real `cargo tauri dev` run would only restate them. Caveat: a real run against pre-existing `localStorage` could display a persisted name and *mask* the fresh-install bug.

---

## Blockers

1. Add Worktree is in the titlebar (`Sidebar.tsx:169`); tests at `Sidebar.test.tsx:95,245,276` encode the wrong behavior and must be inverted.
2. No per-project-row Add Worktree button — the `group/project` hook at `Sidebar.tsx:204` is orphaned.
3. `App.tsx:52` hardcodes `workspaceId: "default"` — no frontend path can surface the derived ID.
4. No IPC command exposes `WorkspaceRegistry::list()` — prerequisite for criterion 3.
5. `lib.rs:152-154` still registers `"default"`, masking the defect.
6. Assertion weakness: neither `Sidebar.test.tsx:262` nor `App.test.tsx` verifies *which* project is targeted; wrong-project routing would go undetected even after the button lands.

No pre-existing failures in the files I ran — all 53 tests pass. The failure is implemented-vs-specified behavior, not test health.
